svg.text: Caching in fux -- one plane, two writers, two readers
No new cache. Python's .fux/runtime/ IS the shared cache; Node reads it and builds it
byte for byte. W-242: all three tiers BUILT and closed 2026-10-03.
0 - THE ONLY INPUT: THE COMMITTED INDEX. NOTHING IN .fux/runtime/ FEEDS ANYTHING BUT A QUERY.
256 shard buckets (constants.toml [index] shards). One line per document: right for git, wrong for querying.
The build reads these and nothing else (SR-T1-ACCELERATOR d1), so rm -rf .fux/runtime is always safe.
Statistics about documents, never the documents (L3). Written by Python's `fux ingest` only.
1 - TWO WRITERS, ONE LOCK, ONE OUTPUT
derive/_build.py (511 lines) -- the reference writer. Asserts both raw-byte
invariants per record (d7) and refuses to build rather than write a plane the
scan could disagree with. ingest builds it too; --no-accelerator leaves it alone.
The stamp is written LAST, after every other file.
node/src/derive/build.mjs (330 lines) -- _build.py's twin; every serializer is
json.dumps reproduced in compat/pyjson.mjs. Same input, same invariants, same
refusals, same write order. Node's first and only write verb. No read verb builds.
ingest stays Python's: Node has no decoders (SR-NODE-SEARCH d11).
O_CREAT|O_EXCL, body {"pid": N} (SR-LOCKS). maintain/runner.py and runner.mjs (narrowed to
acquire). One writer at a time, whichever runtime: a Python ingest and a Node build exclude
each other. A malformed lock reads as HELD; nothing breaks a lock automatically.
every file except stamp.json -- this repo,
2 - THE PLANE: .fux/runtime/ -- GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE. PYTHON'S LAYOUT IS THE CONTRACT; W-242 MOVED NO FILE (fux.runtime.v9)
id, loc, title, flen, archived, superseded, mtime, alen
n, RAW total_flen, total_anchor_len -- never weighted
the graph plane. Both builds write it; both readers read
it when fresh (Fork A, W-259). ensure_ascii, insertion order
docs_fields, counts, a sha per committed shard
[size, mtime_ns] per shard. WRITTEN LAST. The freshness key;
the one file excluded from byte-identity
Candidates and statistics only -- never a score. Both readers hand what they read to the same rank(), so the plane can make a query fast and cannot make it different.
Beside the plane under runtime/, not part of it: write.lock, fetch-cache/, ingest-log.jsonl, inspect/, trace/, and CACHEDIR.TAG (SR-CACHEDIR-TAG) -- which Node's store/fuxdir.mjs writes too.
3 - TWO READERS, ONE FRESHNESS TEST -- the test is also the graph plane's (d19)
schema and docs_fields match, shard count matches, and every shard's
[size, mtime_ns] equals stamp.json. Stat only -- no hashing (doctor re-hashes, W-246).
The same test, transcribed. mtime_ns is ~1.79e18, past 2^53:
statSync(p, {bigint: true}) or it never matches -- silently.
ranked_by: accelerator | scan. --fast opts in; mcp takes the plane when fresh.
ranked_by: accelerator | scan, truthfully -- the arm compares the key now.
same ids, same order, scores equal after round(9) -- in all four paths. Not fresh is never an error. Node at 10k docs: ~0.13 s scan -> ~0.09 s plane.
4 - THE OTHER CACHES -- SR-CACHE's two cache FETCHES (unchanged), the acquired plane, and the resident index (W-249, 2026-10-04)
In memory, one process. The content
address is IN the key, so a hit is the
fetch's own bytes or it is not a hit.
and Node's fux mcp (Resident) hold the
loaded INPUT across calls, keyed on the
stamp digest + every shard's size and

exact repeats; a key long enough to

RULED OUT with Tier 2 (d24): no read
verb builds -- a read verb that builds
is a writer (SR-LOCKS d2). A missing
plane is a scan, not a side effect;
Node reads a fresh graph.json, its own
or Python's; rebuilds in memory other-

6 - WHAT HOLDS THEM EQUAL -- a second writer is a second thing to keep true
The differential law, extended by W-242 -- and measured
query lanes: Node-plane = Node-scan = Python-plane on candidates, (n, total_wlen, df) and ordering -- 0 discordant on this repo, rung-10000, the adversarial index
build lane: diff -r Node-built vs Python-built, excluding stamp.json -- then each runtime answers from the OTHER's plane at 0 discordant
unit binds: one .idx fixture (tests/derive/idx-fixture.*) read by both suites · a shard-read counter (node/test/shard-reads.test.mjs) · graph.json keeps ensure_ascii +
insertion order, the rest sort keys · node/test/graph-read.test.mjs, read vs rebuild · node/test/resident.test.mjs holds the resident key
The arm NEVER takes Node's graph.json read: FUX_GRAPH_REBUILD=1 on every Node child (tests/test_differential_arm.py fails a spawn without it), and every CI arm job runs `fux build` first.
